summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for confusion and hypoglycemia following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Initial evaluation revealed normal liver function and no structural brain abnormalities on MRI and EEG. Ammonia levels fluctuated, peaking at 52, with post-prandial confusion and tremors after a high-protein meal, suggesting a possible urea cycle disorder. Endocrinology evaluated hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia but found normal insulin and C-peptide during fasting; symptoms were attributed to dumping syndrome. The patient remained on continuous tube feeds, avoided oral intake, and was transitioned to NutriHep formula. Rifaximin was continued, and follow-up was arranged for pending urea cycle and pro-insulin results. She improved clinically and was discharged home in stable condition.
problems: Other complications of other bariatric procedure
